[b]April 3, 2028: Office for Pan-Shamatine Affairs[/b]

Mr. Fring, this would be our first meeting since I came into office, would this be correct? asked the shah, seated once more in the patio with Edis, Cahit, and the Director for the Office of Pan-Shamatine Affairs, Gustavo Fring.

Yes, unfortunately, our office has been woefully neglected, replied the balding bureaucrat Fring.

You do understand why? asked Cahit, leaning forward with a frown.

Yes, this administration has woefully neglected our Shamatine neighbours, in favor of a Yzakastan first motion, replied Fring.

That is correct, intoned Cahit, And do you know why? he asked, getting slightly louder.

Cahit, calm please, stated the Shah with a nervous look at Cahits jowls. 

I do not know, sir prelate, replied Fring.

It is because, the world seeks to steal, to grab, to take, and the moment the world gets ahold of our unique system, began Cahit.

They what? asked Fring.

THEY INVADE, THEY COLONISE, THEY DEMAND THAT WE FIT THEIR SYSTEMS, THEIR MODELS! declared Cahit, trembling and slapping the table with emphasis.

THe shah winced and intoned, He has a point, Fring, waggling his finger.

Thank you your honour, smiled Cahit chuckling.

But sir, opening further to international interests, and even participating in the Pan Shamatine Pact, or the Shamatine Security Pact as it is, would greatly aide in lowering the national debt, said Fring.

Yes, but then we have foreigners flooding our streets, said Cahit.

Mr. Prelate, of you of all people should greatly desire such a thing, replied Fring with a snort, causing Cahit to raise an eyebrow.

Please Mr. Fring, the prelate is a sensitive man, said the shah.

The prelate is a dangerous man, mr. president, Replied Fring.

The prelate is sitting at this table, Mr. Fring, replied Cahit quietly.

Can we return to the topic at hand? asked Edis with a hint of frustration in his voice.

Thank you Edis, smiled Cahit, looking at the shah, When will the pastries get here? he asked.

Uh I do not know, I wasnt aware thered be any, replied the Shah with a shrug.

Now, as I was saying, Fring continued, Weve already taken a big leap forward in joining or asking to join PETROX, 

So why not take it the full platter, replied Cahit sarcastically, Bunch of jam that is, he snorted.

Precisely, clapped Fring.

Gustavo, are you aware of the legislative initiative needed for these plans? asked Edis.

Mr. Speaker, I am aware, which is why I am bringing this under the war powers resolution, skips the legislature, goes straight to national referendum, replied Fring.

Cahit snorted, You debase the noble war powers resolution, 

It is a reasonable plan, replied Fring.

It is a disgrace to the war powers resolution, sir, which is a descendant of the Firman, which the glorious shahs of the caliphate who rode across the steppes, stated Cahit with a flourish of his hands.

A firman sir, hasnt been issued in nearly a century, scoffed Fring.

Gentlemen, we arent getting here anywhere, replied the shah with a sigh, Mr. Fring, if you can submit your idea via a folio, and we will review it, thank you,
